messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: bug while using geom_ribbon?
parts:
No, not a bug, but rather a (very common!) misunderstanding of what xlim/ylim do. Basically, xlim/ylim throw away data, not scale axes; I suggest reading the examples in ?coord_cartesian.

Ben


On Wed, Oct 24, 2012 at 4:59 AM, Robert Reijntjes <r.rei...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,

I'm trying to plot some lines with a region around the lines.

I'm using the following command:
limits <- aes(ymax = upper, ymin=lower,group=patient)
ggplot(nremw,aes(x=min,y=HR,colour=patient, group=interaction(pm,patient)))+
  geom_line() +
  geom_ribbon(limits,alpha=0.2, colour=NA) +
  theme_bw()
this produces the following plot:

When I use the same command but now with ylim:

ggplot(nremw,aes(x=min,y=HR,colour=patient, group=interaction(pm,patient)))+
  geom_line() +
  geom_ribbon(limits,alpha=0.2, colour=NA) +
  ylim(45.85) +
  theme_bw()

Notice that a part of the grey area in the lower left corner is missing.

It must be a bug. I hope I've given enough information to solve it.

Greetings

  Robert

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: bug while using geom_ribbon?
parts:
Not a bug. It's doing what you tell it to, but it's just not what you expect. When you set a limit, it removes data that is below your limit, which includes your loess standard error. 

Please see the first few examples here on how to do what you want.:
http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/coord_cartesian.html
